nodes.text: At lunch, Emily sits with Kimi at a table at the edge of the cafeteria.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: I can't wait until we're cool enough to sit at the Center Table.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Center Table?

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: Yes. Hello? Didn't I tell you about the solar system of popularity?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Uh...

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: It's simple. Look.
Kimi points out a nearby table, filled with nerds moving plastic pieces over an ornately decorated board.

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: All I need to do is roll a 16 or higher and the Chainmail of Azgura is mine!

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: At the outer rim of the solar system are the nerds and outcasts... They're like the Pluto of the solar system.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Got it.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: One level in...
Kimi points to a table filled with a mix of students...

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: And you have your emo kids and drama hounds.

nodes.speaker: Jenna
nodes.text: How dare they feed us this tripe! Not as long as I'm at this school!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: More like Jupiter or Saturn?

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: Exactly, lots of gravity, but not the center of the universe. Even if they think they are.
Emily's gaze settles on a table in the center of the cafeteria, bathed in a swath of sunlight.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: The Sun. Where only the most popular kids dare to sit.
Emily sees Dominique and Lindsay sitting there, but she tries not to let it bother her...
One of the nerds comes up to Emily.

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: Let me guess... You're a Dark-Elf thief, right? I can always spot fellow gamers.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I don't, uh, steal things.

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: Forgive Dex. He's not used to conversations with actual females. Actually, we were just curious if you want to sit with us.

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: Since we're stuck together at the outer limits. I'm Kevin, by the way. Kevin Delucca.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Uh, sure... We'd be happy to...
Kimi grabs Emily's arm, holding her back.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: Actually, we have some private matters to discuss.

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: Sure.
Kimi pulls Emily away.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: What's up with you? They seemed like nice guys.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: Emily, Emily, Emily. Don't be so naive. Right now, as freshmen, we're a fresh commodity here.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: Sure, we're not popular `yet,` but I'd like to think that one day we could be. If we start hanging out with guys like that, it's never going to happen.
nodes.text_bbcode: Sure, we're not popular [color=#3b78e2][i]yet,[/i][/color] but I'd like to think that one day we could be. If we start hanging out with guys like that, it's never going to happen.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: We'll be branded nerd girls for life!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Okay... Sure. I'm too hungry to talk much anyway.
While Kimi nibbles on a bagel with a thin layer of cottage cheese, Emily reaches into her bag and pulls out her lunch...
A bowl of yogurt, a whey protein shake, orange juice, half a loaf of whole wheat bread covered in almond butter...
...Milk, almonds, vitamins, raisins, two bananas, and a pack of sliced turkey.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: You sure you don't want a couple of pizzas to go with that?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I guess I'm not that hungry. I had a big breakfast.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: I bet you did. How many calories a day are you up to now?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: 8,000. But you should see how `guy` swimmers eat. I mean, most people don't regulate their percentage of carbs, proteins, and fats correctly.
nodes.text_bbcode: 8,000. But you should see how [color=#3b78e2][i]guy[/i][/color] swimmers eat. I mean, most people don't regulate their percentage of carbs, proteins, and fats correctly.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: You'd be surprised how even at the highest level, a lot of the guys are just eating deep-fried turkeys and cheese sandwiches.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Some of them eat like 12,000 or 13,000 calories a day, which is probably on the high end of what they should be...

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: Oh, yeah. `That` would be a lot. I mean, 8,000 calories is barely anything... For a polar bear.
nodes.text_bbcode: Oh, yeah. [color=#3b78e2][i]That[/i][/color] would be a lot. I mean, 8,000 calories is barely anything... For a polar bear.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: It's so unfair. If I even eat like two extra cookies, my jeans don't fit anymore. My mom says our family has slow metab...
Kimi's words are cut off by a chant from the Center Table...

nodes.speaker: Zach
nodes.text: Eat! Eat! Eat!

nodes.speaker: Phil
nodes.text: Eat! Eat! Eat!
In the middle of a circle of popular students, Dominique `is` actually wolfing down pizzas.
nodes.text_bbcode: In the middle of a circle of popular students, Dominique [b]is[/b] actually wolfing down pizzas.

nodes.text: As she polishes off another slice, the chant changes...

nodes.speaker: Zach
nodes.text: Dom-i-nique! Dom-i-nique!

nodes.speaker: Phil
nodes.text: Dom-i-nique! Dom-i-nique!
Across the cafeteria, Emily sees Dominique's half-brother Cameron watching the eating display with a wry smile.
Dominique holds the empty pizza boxes over her head, and the crowd cheers!

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: Woo!
Two guys from the crowd break off and start walking toward Emily's table...

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Dude, a hot chick who can pack away that much pizza is basically a goddess. I'm all over that.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Yeah, sure.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: You okay, man? You seem, I dunno... Off or something.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Just bored. One day back and I'm already bored. Maybe there `is` something wrong with me.
nodes.text_bbcode: Just bored. One day back and I'm already bored. Maybe there [color=#e23b3b][i]is[/i][/color] something wrong with me.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I just can't get excited about a girl putting away pizzas.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Are you crazy? Dominique is basically the perfect woman. She's like a guy... But in an incredibly hot girl's body!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: And did you hear that she watches pro sports on TV when she runs on the treadmill... For six hours?!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: I started fantasizing about her listing quarterback ratings while she wrestled me to the ground and...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Okay, okay, I get it. But can you imagine going on dates with her?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: She'd totally empty your wallet every time you went out for dinner. I'll stick to girls who `only want a slice or two.`
nodes.text_bbcode: She'd totally empty your wallet every time you went out for dinner. I'll stick to girls who [color=#e23b3b][i]only want a slice or two.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Whatever, man. I still say she's hot. I could see her perfect abs `through her dress.` Where did she even `put` those pizzas?
nodes.text_bbcode: Whatever, man. I still say she's hot. I could see her perfect abs [color=#e23b3b][i]through her dress.[/i][/color] Where did she even [color=#e23b3b][i]put[/i][/color] those pizzas?

nodes.text: Meanwhile...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: They're coming this way!

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: So?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: So?! That one guy's hot! And did you hear what he just said?! 'Only a slice or two.'
Emily eyes all the food currently laid out on the table.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Help me!
Kimi doesn't hesitate. In rapid succession, both girls clear the food off the table!
Ben and Spencer walk by just as Emily hides the almonds in her lap and casually puts her hands back on the table...
Suddenly, Ben stops!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh, hey. Are you okay?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: He's `actually` talking to me. Don't freak out. Don't embarrass yourself.
nodes.text_bbcode: He's [color=#3b78e2][i]actually[/i][/color] talking to me. Don't freak out. Don't embarrass yourself.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Uh... I'm... Fine.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: It's just... Well, you have your hand in a bowl of yogurt.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Oh. That's. Yes. That's, uh... I burned my hand on... A beaker. In chemistry. And the yogurt is supposed to help the skin heal.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Chemistry, huh?
He chuckles to himself as he and his friend walk away...

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: I `can't` believe it! You were just talking to Ben Kale!
nodes.text_bbcode: I [color=#3b78e2][i]can't[/i][/color] believe it! You were just talking to Ben Kale!

nodes.text: Later, in Emily's Honors History class...

nodes.speaker: Mr. Russell
nodes.text: Technically, the administration has deemed this textbook too difficult for first year students.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I can't believe I actually talked to Ben Kale...

nodes.speaker: Mr. Russell
nodes.text: They even went so far as to ban the book depository from passing them out to anyone with a Twin Branches ID.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I can't believe I actually talked to Ben Kale... With my hand in a bowl of yogurt...

nodes.speaker: Mr. Russell
nodes.text: Luckily, I have a friend at a used bookstore who picked me up my own personal set for pennies on the dollar!
Mr. Russell stops for a moment, glaring at the class...

nodes.speaker: Mr. Russell
nodes.text: But be warned! There are no replacement copies. Lose your book, and I dock you a letter grade. Worse than that, though, you won't have a book to read.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I wonder if Ben thinks I'm completely crazy... Or just a little bit crazy?

nodes.speaker: Mr. Russell
nodes.text: Get the message? Hold onto this book as if your very life depends on it! In many ways, it does.
He drops a textbook on Emily's desk with a loud slam, startling her! He glowers down at her...

nodes.speaker: Mr. Russell
nodes.text: Welcome to Honors History. Pay attention!
Then he turns back to the board and shouts...

nodes.speaker: Mr. Russell
nodes.text: Lesson One: The Fertile Crescent!
Emily takes a deep breath.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Why didn't I just take regular classes with Kimi?
After school, in the aquatic center, the tension finally drains from Emily's body.
She feels at peace, swimming through the water, the tight fabric of her swimsuit hugging her like a long-lost sister.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Other girls are snacking, watching TV on their couches, texting their friends... But not me.
She slaps the far wall of the pool, deftly changing directions underwater and pushing back the other way.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Sara's nickname was 'The Machine'. Perfect mechanics. No junk food, no parties, no boyfriends.
Emily slaps the near wall hard, and the worry starts to leave. She heads out for another lap.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: What a day...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: First the ID photo, then Dominique, no classes with Kimi...
`Slap!`
nodes.text_bbcode: [b]Slap![/b]

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I mistook Miss Prez for a student, Mr Russell's textbook is apparently a holy relic, and then there was the incident with Ben...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: `The yogurt is supposed to help the skin heal.` Yeah, real smooth, Em.
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#3b78e2][i]The yogurt is supposed to help the skin heal.[/i][/color] Yeah, real smooth, Em.

nodes.text: `Slap!`
nodes.text_bbcode: [b]Slap![/b]

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: At least... At least I didn't see Nick Brown...
As Emily reaches the wall again she stops and rests her arms on the pool's edge. Her father is there, watching her from a diving block, his legs dangling over the water.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Why are you in your race gear? We bought you that resistance suit for a reason. You've got to build muscle, or you're never going to lower your split times.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: It's my first day here. I just want to relax.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: And you think Dominique is relaxing in that big indoor pool her parents built her? Or any of the other girls?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Fine. Fine, Dad. I'll change.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: `Coach.` You'll call me `'Coach'` while we're at school. Just like the other girls.
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#e23b3b][i]Coach.[/i][/color] You'll call me [color=#e23b3b][i]'Coach'[/i][/color] while we're at school. Just like the other girls.

nodes.text: His eyes settle on Emily's resting arms. Instinctively, she pushes off, treading water.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: One other thing, I almost forgot. A reporter from `Swimmer's Monthly` is coming by in a couple of weeks to do a story on you and Dominique.
nodes.text_bbcode: One other thing, I almost forgot. A reporter from [color=#e23b3b][i]Swimmer's Monthly[/i][/color] is coming by in a couple of weeks to do a story on you and Dominique.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: It's a chance to get your name out there, and it's good practice for later.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Unfortunately, part of being an athlete of your caliber means dealing with the press.
Emily tries to make eye contact with her father, hoping he'll see how much she doesn't want to do the interview, but instead...
He looks at the list of names and times on the far wall... At the name and time in the bottom corner...
`Sara Kessler 50M backstroke, 28.3`
nodes.text_bbcode: [b]Sara Kessler 50M backstroke, 28.3[/b]

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: You're on the right track.
He stands up, walking away from Emily...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Now get to the locker room and put on your resistance gear. We've only got two hours before this place closes.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Two hours of this... And then a four-mile run...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Still, better than getting into a car...
Emily climbs out of the pool and heads toward the locker room.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I wish there weren't any cars... Just boats, like those gondolas in Venice. Boats are safe.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Boats don't go fast. Boats rock gently on the waves...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Boats don't spin out of control because some stupid teenage boy is behind the wheel.
The next day, right before swim practice...
Emily is walking toward the aquatic center, when she sees Ben and Spencer running her direction, `fast.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Emily is walking toward the aquatic center, when she sees Ben and Spencer running her direction, [b]fast.[/b]

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Mission accomplished, Kale. Dominique is totally going to freak. I owe you one.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Are you kidding? This is the most fun I've had all year!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Better split up. Your place in thirty?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I'll see you there.
Ben notices Emily...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Hey, it's you... Yogurt.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: My name isn't Yogurt.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Sure. Look. Do me a favor. If school security comes by, tell them I ran that way, okay?
He points down one of the hallways before stepping into the girls' restroom.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: There's no one in there, right?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I don't...
But before Emily can answer, the door closes.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Great. If I wait here to talk to Ben, I'll end up late for practice, and my dad will be even more mad at me. Why is life this hard?
A minute later, a stocky man in a school security uniform huffs his way up to her.

nodes.speaker: Officer Monte
nodes.text: Hey, you. See anyone run by?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Uh...

nodes.speaker: Officer Monte
nodes.text: A correct response would be either 'yes' or 'no'.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Well, a couple of guys ran off that way.
Emily points in the hallway Ben had indicated a moment ago, and Monte runs off in that direction.
A moment later, the bathroom door cracks open.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: He gone?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Yeah.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Wow. Girls write `way` dirtier stuff on bathroom walls than guys do. I didn't see you mentioned anywhere, though. Too bad.
nodes.text_bbcode: Wow. Girls write [color=#e23b3b][i]way[/i][/color] dirtier stuff on bathroom walls than guys do. I didn't see you mentioned anywhere, though. Too bad.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Well, most people don't call me 'Yogurt'.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I know. But 'Emily Kessler'? That's just so... I don't know... Boring. 'Yogurt' suits you way better.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: He... He knows my name!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh, Yogurt?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: That's not my name!
From down the hall, an unmistakable voice yells out!

nodes.speaker: Officer Monte
nodes.text: Hey! You! Stop right there!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: That would be my cue to leave. Maybe I'll see you again sometime.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Maybe. Anyway, I'd better get to practice.
As Ben takes off running, he shouts over his shoulder.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: You never know when swim practice might get canceled! I'll see you around!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: So... Ben Kale knows my name `and` was totally flirting with me!
nodes.text_bbcode: So... Ben Kale knows my name [color=#3b78e2][i]and[/i][/color] was totally flirting with me!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: But what did he mean about swim practice being canceled?
A few minutes later, Emily stands beside her father and the rest of the swim team, looking into the pool...
A cloud of bright green color is blossoming at the far end and spreading its way toward them.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: What happened?

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: Apparently some `boys` dumped like thirty vials of green food coloring into the pool. And maybe some other stuff, too, based on the smell.
nodes.text_bbcode: Apparently some [color=#3b78e2][i]boys[/i][/color] dumped like thirty vials of green food coloring into the pool. And maybe some other stuff, too, based on the smell.

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: I think it smells yummy. I kind of want to drink it.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: No one's drinking it! No one's so much as dipping a pinky toe in there until we drain the thing and pump in fresh water.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Who knows what chemicals are in there? I'm not getting sued by some mother whose daughter's skin turns green.

nodes.speaker: Lindsay
nodes.text: So, does that mean practice is canceled?

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Absolutely not. The school still has a weight room, doesn't it? Unless someone turned that green too.
The girls are headed back to the locker room when Emily's father stops her and Dominique.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: You two, wait. I'm pulling you out for the first hour to talk to a reporter from `Swimmer's Monthly.`
nodes.text_bbcode: You two, wait. I'm pulling you out for the first hour to talk to a reporter from [color=#e23b3b][i]Swimmer's Monthly.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: I believe I mentioned she'd be coming? She's waiting in the hall.
Emily and Dominique both give each other the same look: `This might not be a good idea.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Emily and Dominique both give each other the same look: [b]This might not be a good idea.[/b]

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: She's talking to us together?

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Is there a problem with that?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Yes. There's a big problem: Dominique and I hate each other!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Uh... No problem at all, Coach.
In an empty classroom...

nodes.speaker: Reporter
nodes.text: How much time do you spend practicing?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Every day.

nodes.speaker: Reporter
nodes.text: And Dominique, how is your life different than a typical high school student's?

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: Oh, I'm just a normal high school kid.

nodes.speaker: Reporter
nodes.text: Uh huh. What gives you two a leg up on all the other young swimmers out there?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: We just want it more.
The reporter nods and slides her chair closer.

nodes.speaker: Reporter
nodes.text: Okay. Now for the juicy stuff. As two of the top swimmers in your age group in the nation...

nodes.speaker: Reporter
nodes.text: ...Do you ever find the rivalry spilling out from the pool into the outside world?
Emily shares a nervous look with Dominique. `This isn't a puff piece.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Emily shares a nervous look with Dominique. [b]This isn't a puff piece.[/b]

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I can imagine the headline now... `Potential Olympians in the Water, Spoiled Brats on Dry Land.`
nodes.text_bbcode: I can imagine the headline now... [color=#3b78e2][i]Potential Olympians in the Water, Spoiled Brats on Dry Land.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Uh, outside the pool...

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: We're totally friends. I mean, not BFF's or anything, but we're definitely close.

nodes.speaker: Reporter
nodes.text: Is that right? Several people that I talked to seemed to think that...

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: I think it's hard for other people to understand the kind of competitive spirit that gets into you when you swim at the highest level.

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: But if it comes across as anything but an in-the-pool rivalry, that's just wrong.
The reporter frowns and deletes some of her notes from her computer... Then she looks up and smiles.

nodes.speaker: Reporter
nodes.text: Dominique, thank you so much for your time. If you don't mind, I've got a few more questions for your 'friend'.
Dominique stands, a strange look on her face.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: She's relieved to be done with the interview, but worried about what I'll say once she's gone.

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: Not a problem. Thanks `so` much for the questions.
nodes.text_bbcode: Not a problem. Thanks [color=#3b78e2][i]so[/i][/color] much for the questions.

nodes.text: She shoots Emily a glare. `Don't screw this up.`
nodes.text_bbcode: She shoots Emily a glare. [b]Don't screw this up.[/b]

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: See you later, Em.
She leaves. The reporter smiles at Emily, with a look that Emily can't read.

nodes.speaker: Reporter
nodes.text: Emily, it's clear to me that you're the real story here.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Huh?

nodes.speaker: Reporter
nodes.text: I'm talking about your motivations. Yes, clearly you and Dominique both want to win. But with you it goes deeper.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Where is she going with this? Is this about Sara?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I have no idea what you're talking about.

nodes.speaker: Reporter
nodes.text: Fine. I should be more direct. Emily, you come from a family of successful swimmers...
She trails off, as if hoping Emily will get the hint. But Emily ignores her and stares out the window.

nodes.speaker: Reporter
nodes.text: Your father, Coach Kessler, is of course a former Olympian, and your sister Sara set a national juniors record at the age of sixteen before her tragic death last year.

nodes.speaker: Reporter
nodes.text: What's it like trying to live up to such a legacy?
Emily feels like she's just been punched in the gut. She tries to speak, but nothing comes.

nodes.speaker: Reporter
nodes.text: Emily?
Emily sits completely still. She can feel her hands shaking.

nodes.speaker: Reporter
nodes.text: Emily, help me out here. How does it feel to have that kind of...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: How do you think it feels?

nodes.speaker: Reporter
nodes.text: Well, I don't know, sweetie. That's why I'm asking you.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: It's just... It's just so stupid. I could sit here and explain how I can't get into a pool without thinking of my older sister...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: ...Or how I follow the `exact` same training regimens my dad designed for her, even her sleep schedule, down to the minute!
nodes.text_bbcode: ...Or how I follow the [color=#3b78e2][i]exact[/i][/color] same training regimens my dad designed for her, even her sleep schedule, down to the minute!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Or how before I ever check my times against Dominique's, I check them against Sara's.
The reporter types furiously, trying to catch every word.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Sara could have won medals too. Way more than my dad ever did. But she didn't get to.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: And if I don't work just as hard as she would have, if I don't live up to that, I mean, what was it all for?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: And now here you are asking all these questions about her, just trying to turn all of this into... Into some kind of `story.`
nodes.text_bbcode: And now here you are asking all these questions about her, just trying to turn all of this into... Into some kind of [color=#3b78e2][i]story.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Reporter
nodes.text: You've got me all wrong. Of course I'm looking for the best story, but I'm on your side. I'm going to make you a hero.

nodes.speaker: Reporter
nodes.text: I'm going to make you a star.
A few weeks later...
Emily's father flops `Swimmer's Monthly` down on the dining room table.
nodes.text_bbcode: Emily's father flops [b]Swimmer's Monthly[/b] down on the dining room table.

nodes.text: Emily's on the cover, tearing through the water next to a bold headline about fulfilling the legacy of her sister.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Congratulations. You're famous.
Emily feels sick to her stomach.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Dad? The cover? Really? Now everyone at school's going to think I'm... I'm...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: A great swimmer. But I wouldn't worry. I don't think too many kids at the high school read `Swimmer's Monthly.`
nodes.text_bbcode: A great swimmer. But I wouldn't worry. I don't think too many kids at the high school read [color=#e23b3b][i]Swimmer's Monthly.[/i][/color]

nodes.text: That weekend...

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: This is awesome! I can't believe the article made it into the school paper!
Kimi lies on Emily's bed and flips through the article...

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: She made you sound like a rock star or something!

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: And the best part is... Dominique only got like two paragraphs!
Emily winces.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Great. So now Dominique is going to totally hate me.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: Aww. Don't be so upset. She already hated you.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Why couldn't that stupid reporter have just left me alone?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I haven't even won anything. This is just... Too much attention.
Kimi looks up from the article.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: You're joking, right? This is the best thing that's ever happened to us. You're going to be totally famous now.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: Forget sitting in the corner of the cafeteria. Forget boys completely ignoring us. Forget never getting invited to parties.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: We're in!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Not to burst your bubble or anything, but it's just a stupid story. No one at school's going to read it.
Emily closes the article on her computer and logs into Faceplace.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: Em, don't do this. You `always` do this. Something good happens, and you find a way to...
nodes.text_bbcode: Em, don't do this. You [color=#3b78e2][i]always[/i][/color] do this. Something good happens, and you find a way to...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Kimi...

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: No! Don't interrupt. What I'm saying is you always find a way to take some awesome thing that just happened and make it look like a complete...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Kimi!

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: What?!
Emily turns her laptop screen so Kimi can see it.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I just logged onto Faceplace.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: Yeah. And?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: And I have 160 new friend requests.
We hope you enjoyed this preview of `Surviving High School,` the novel, coming soon!
nodes.text_bbcode: We hope you enjoyed this preview of [b]Surviving High School,[/b] the novel, coming soon!

nodes.text: Want to find out more about Emily's newfound fame? Her competition with Dominique? And her crush on Ben Kale?
Follow Emily's story in our upcoming novel, `Surviving High School` by M. Doty!
nodes.text_bbcode: Follow Emily's story in our upcoming novel, [b]Surviving High School[/b] by M. Doty!

nodes.text: Help us make the book a hit and `pre-order` it online on `August 24, 2012!`
nodes.text_bbcode: Help us make the book a hit and [b]pre-order[/b] it online on [b]August 24, 2012![/b]

nodes.text: See you next week!
The days pass, and Emily falls into a kind of routine, a routine that isn't broken until...
At lunch one day, she notices Dominique and Lindsay whispering and giggling at a `different` table.
nodes.text_bbcode: At lunch one day, she notices Dominique and Lindsay whispering and giggling at a [b]different[/b] table.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Not sitting at the Center Table? Whispering and giggling? Something's up.
Emily alters her route and walks slowly past, catching only two words...

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: ... Ben Kale...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Come on... What am I supposed to do now?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I could sit at this empty table right here, but I'll be totally obvious!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Where's Kimi when you need her?

nodes.speaker: Lindsay
nodes.text: What happened to you at the party Friday? It was like, one second I was getting you some ice, then the next... Poof!

nodes.speaker: Lindsay
nodes.text: You and Ben were gone.
At the words, 'You and Ben' Emily reflexively sits at the empty table.

nodes.speaker: Lindsay
nodes.text: And `then,` you didn't respond to `any` of my texts all weekend? `Tell me` you made out with Ben and ran off to Vegas to get married or something!
nodes.text_bbcode: And [color=#3b78e2][i]then,[/i][/color] you didn't respond to [color=#3b78e2][i]any[/i][/color] of my texts all weekend? [color=#3b78e2][i]Tell me[/i][/color] you made out with Ben and ran off to Vegas to get married or something!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Ben and Dominique making out? Please no! Please no! Please no...

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: I wish. I was `totally` ready to jump him when we got to the bedroom. But then Spencer was waiting there!
nodes.text_bbcode: I wish. I was [color=#3b78e2][i]totally[/i][/color] ready to jump him when we got to the bedroom. But then Spencer was waiting there!

nodes.text: Emily's shoulders relax.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Thank you, Spencer!

nodes.speaker: Lindsay
nodes.text: Spencer? The guy who got his hair cut in the shape of a lizard? That Spencer?

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: I don't get why Ben is friends with that guy. `Such` a tool.
nodes.text_bbcode: I don't get why Ben is friends with that guy. [color=#3b78e2][i]Such[/i][/color] a tool.

nodes.speaker: Lindsay
nodes.text: Yeah, he's definitely a fixer-upper and a half. His body's not so bad, though.

nodes.speaker: Lindsay
nodes.text: If you like, you know, body-builder type guys.

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: Which I don't. Ben and I had to sit talking to him for like half an hour while he told me about his dad's new landscaping business.

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: `And` he spilled his drink on my cell.
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#3b78e2][i]And[/i][/color] he spilled his drink on my cell.

nodes.speaker: Lindsay
nodes.text: What about Ben? Did anything happen at all?

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: He'd probably have been all over me if Spencer hadn't gotten in the way.

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: I mean, I did catch him checking me out while we were sitting there, before he ended up leaving me alone with Spencer for the rest of the night.

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: I think it's one of those things where he wants to be a good guy and let Spencer have a chance with me first.

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: So all I have to do now is make sure Ben knows I'm interested in `him` and not his friend. Then he'll be all mine.
nodes.text_bbcode: So all I have to do now is make sure Ben knows I'm interested in [color=#3b78e2][i]him[/i][/color] and not his friend. Then he'll be all mine.

nodes.speaker: Lindsay
nodes.text: But wait... Ben never came back to the party.

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: He said he was tired and that he was going to sleep.

nodes.speaker: Lindsay
nodes.text: So he totally just crawled into bed at 11:00 at night in the middle of a party that `he` was throwing?
nodes.text_bbcode: So he totally just crawled into bed at 11:00 at night in the middle of a party that [color=#3b78e2][i]he[/i][/color] was throwing?

nodes.speaker: Lindsay
nodes.text: Isn't that, I don't know, a little psycho or something?

nodes.speaker: Lindsay
nodes.text: I mean, yes, he's uber hot and smart, and his party was pretty awesome, but...
Emily turns, trying to hear the rest of Lindsay's sentence, but she quickly forgets about it.
Over Lindsay's shoulder, she sees `him.` Nick Brown. The one guy she'd been avoiding at all costs.
nodes.text_bbcode: Over Lindsay's shoulder, she sees [b]him.[/b] Nick Brown. The one guy she'd been avoiding at all costs.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: He looks taller. Cuter, even.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: So unfair. My sister's dead, and all Nick has to show for what happened is a growth spurt, a nice haircut, and a cool-looking scar.
Dominique and Lindsay's discussion now sounds muted, far away, distant.

nodes.speaker: Lindsay
nodes.text: ...I guess Ben's got issues or something...
Nick starts taking pictures of random students...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: He looks thinner now...

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: ...Would still totally let him take me to Homecoming...
Nick walks up to another group of students...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Yearbook candids.
They instantly pose for the camera, making silly faces.
Emily turns from him, trying to hide her face.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: He's going to see me! Why did I have to sit here?! Just to listen to a stupid conversation about a stupid party?!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Sara wouldn't have done this... Sara would have been in the gym, or doing her homework... She was The Machine.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: But now... Sara wouldn't ever get to do any of those things again... Because of him.
Nick reaches Dominique and Lindsay's table.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Yearbook.
Emily doesn't turn around. She hears Dominique and Lindsay giggle as they squeeze together. She hears the click of Nick's camera.
She hears his footsteps as he nears her...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Yearbook.
She freezes. Her heart pounds in her chest. This is actually happening.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Yearbook.
Emily turns, ever so slightly... And watches out of the corner of her eye as the blood drains from Nick's face.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: ...Sara?
Emily steels her jaw, grabs her backpack, and walks out of the cafeteria as fast as she can!
She races into the bathroom!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Hearing Sara's name is one thing... But hearing it `from him...`
nodes.text_bbcode: Hearing Sara's name is one thing... But hearing it [color=#3b78e2][i]from him...[/i][/color]

nodes.text: The tears start to fall down Emily's cheeks, but she doesn't wipe them away... The only thing she thinks is...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Sara wouldn't cry.
After school, Emily heads straight to the locker room...
As she's just about done changing into her swimsuit, she overhears some of the other girls as they enter...

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: I heard she was crying at lunch today. Hannah totally heard her sobbing in a bathroom stall.

nodes.speaker: Lindsay
nodes.text: Over a boy you think?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Would they still talk like that if they knew what I had really been crying about?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Probably...

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: As if a boy would even touch her. She's basically not a person. Dating her would be like dating a toaster.

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: She's a robot. A swimbot. Oh! I think `someone` just got a new nickname!
nodes.text_bbcode: She's a robot. A swimbot. Oh! I think [color=#3b78e2][i]someone[/i][/color] just got a new nickname!

nodes.text: The girls turn the corner and stop talking when they see Emily.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Hello...
Dominique adopts a robot voice.

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: Hel-lo. I. Am. Swim. Bot. Hel-lo. Human.

nodes.speaker: Lindsay
nodes.text: Bwahahaha!

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: Take. Me. To. Your. Leader.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: That's an alien. Not a robot.

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: Alien. Does. Not. Compute.
More girls arrive, and the laughing gets louder.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Just stop it, okay?

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: Stop. What? Need. Fuel. Give. Me. Weird. Almond. Butter. Flax. Seed.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Keep it together. Don't let her know that it gets to you...

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: Nobody. Asks me. Out. Why don't. Human boys. Like me?
A strong voice booms out from behind Emily.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I haven't seen you with a whole lot of boyfriends, either, Dom. I think I'm starting to see why.
Sam is tall to begin with, taller still when she stands on a nearby bench, towering over the other girls.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Listen up, ladies. Save your insults for other teams, like Wilson High. You two are teammates.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: You're worried Emily might be better in the pool? Work harder.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: You think you're so hot that you want to offer Emily some dating advice? Get your own boyfriend first.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: And don't flatter yourself. I've seen you getting out of the water, and without that mountain of concealer...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: ...You look like a 'before' model in an acne cream ad.
Sam hops down from the bench, pulling her swimsuit from her locker while the other girls stand there, shocked. Sam turns and glares at them.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: We're done here now. Go.
The girls scatter.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Thanks.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Don't think I'm your friend...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: You know, you remind me of your sister. I mean, you look just like her.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Yeah, we used to get that a lot...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Were you and Sara... Friends?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I wouldn't say that. We... Never mind.
Sam tucks her hair under her swim cap.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Hair. What a hassle. You ever just think of cutting it all off?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Not really.
Sam closes her locker shut, nods at Emily, and walks away.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Why did she change the subject so suddenly?
A few minutes later, Emily swims with fury, imagining that every time she slaps the wall, it's Dominique's face.
After a few laps, she realizes that it isn't Dominique who has upset her... She replays her conversation with Sam in her head...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Were you and Sara... Friends?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I wouldn't say that. We... Never mind.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Was Sam Sara's swimming rival? It had to be that... Sara didn't have a life outside of the pool. She was The Machine.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: ...Right?
Emily's aching arms wake her from her trance. She stops at the pool's edge.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Oh no. I didn't realize how hard I was swimming, and there's still two hours of practice left!
A shadow falls over her, and she looks up to see her father...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Kessler! What do you think you're doing?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Kessler? Really?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Just taking a little break... `Coach.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Just taking a little break... [color=#3b78e2][i]Coach.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: And who around here said you could do that? You stop when I tell you to stop.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: But Dad...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: `Coach.`
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#e23b3b][i]Coach.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Fine. Whatever.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: You just bought yourself another hour in the pool.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: But...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: You want to go for two?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: No, sir.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Looks like I won't be getting any special treatment for being the coach's daughter... In fact, it's kind of the opposite.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: That's better.
Emily's dad turns and walks away. In the next lane over, Dominique surfaces.

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: Making trouble already. Eh, Swimbot?
Emily ignores her and gets into position to work on her backstroke.

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: Backstroke's not your race. You might want to, you know, forget about it. Concentrate on some strokes where you actually stand a chance of winning.
Dominique gets into the backstroke position next to Emily.

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: I'm trying to remember... Have you `ever` beaten me at backstroke?
nodes.text_bbcode: I'm trying to remember... Have you [color=#3b78e2][i]ever[/i][/color] beaten me at backstroke?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: You haven't seen me swim it in competition since May.

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: Then I guess you wouldn't mind a little race? There and back?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Not at all.
Emily sees that the rest of the swimmers have stopped and are now watching her and Dominique.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Well, that was stupid. She knows I already overextended myself. She's trying to make me look bad.

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: Three. Two. One.
Emily and Dominique push off simultaneously, gliding through the water. Emily counts the flags as they pass overhead.
Then Emily hears the sound of the other swimmers chanting...

nodes.speaker: Chant
nodes.text: Dom-i-nique! Dom-i-nique!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: How could they all be cheering against me?
A voice answers inside her.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Because you're a machine. Just like your sister was, and no one cheers for the machine...
`Slam!`
nodes.text_bbcode: [b]Slam![/b]

nodes.text: Emily's head collides with the wall, a wave of pain rushing over her.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: `Oof!`
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#3b78e2][i]Oof![/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I can't believe I lost count of the flags! That hasn't happened since elementary school...
Emily stops swimming. There isn't any reason to continue. A few seconds later, Dominique touches the wall, and the other girls cheer!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: It's just practice, Emily. You'll have all year to beat her.
Dominique triumphantly pumps her fist into the air...

nodes.speaker: Dominique
nodes.text: Woo!
That night, at dinner...

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: So... How was work?

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Fine. Except that `one` of the swimmers had a discipline problem and then tried to show off by having a little race...
nodes.text_bbcode: Fine. Except that [color=#e23b3b][i]one[/i][/color] of the swimmers had a discipline problem and then tried to show off by having a little race...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Which she `lost,` by the way.
nodes.text_bbcode: Which she [color=#e23b3b][i]lost,[/i][/color] by the way.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: Well... What about you, Emily?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Fantastic. Except the stupid `coach` made me practice for an extra hour for basically no reason.
nodes.text_bbcode: Fantastic. Except the stupid [color=#3b78e2][i]coach[/i][/color] made me practice for an extra hour for basically no reason.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: Well... It sounds like everyone could use a little cheering up, and I have just the thing!

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: A pint of a certain pair of people's favorite ice cream that may or may not contain delicious dark chocolate fish.
Emily's mouth starts to water.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Chocolate! I haven't had chocolate since... Since...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Not for her. She's already had her 8,000 calories, and that much sugar and fat would be terrible for her system, especially this soon before bedtime.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: Just a few scoops couldn't possibly hurt.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: I said 'no'.
Emily pops a pair of vitamins from the side of her plate and finishes the last of her water.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: It's fine, Mom. He's right. I'm not hungry anyway.
A few hours later... Emily stretches out next to a mountain of homework. Her mom knocks on the door and comes in, holding a coffee mug.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: I brought you some 'tea'.
She winks, handing the mug to Emily. It's filled with ice cream.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: I figured a few hundred calories couldn't hurt. Besides, conditioning is an art, not a science. Even your father says that.
Emily takes the mug and stares at the ice cream, fixated. She presses her finger into it and brings her finger to her lips...
Suddenly, her entire being is focused completely on the taste of chocolatey sweetness.
She takes a deep breath... And hands the mug back to her mother.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Mom. I can't.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: But...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Sara wouldn't have eaten a mug of ice cream.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: Right. Of course.
Emily's mother stays there for a moment, watching the ice cream melt, as if hoping that Emily will change her mind...
But Emily stays silent.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: Well... Good night.
Emily's mother walks away, sadly scooping up some ice cream as she leaves.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I'm sorry, Mom. As much as I disagree with Dad... I still want to win...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I just wish that ice cream hadn't tasted `so` good.
nodes.text_bbcode: I just wish that ice cream hadn't tasted [color=#3b78e2][i]so[/i][/color] good.

nodes.text: Later that night...
Emily checks her Faceplace account.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Thirty online friends... But only one real one...
She gives Kimi a call.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Hey, Kimi!

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: Hey, Em! Sorry I missed you at lunch. I was totally hiding from that Dex guy.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Who?

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: The guy who tried to recruit us for his hyper-nerdy role-playing game. He's like a `total` stalker.
nodes.text_bbcode: The guy who tried to recruit us for his hyper-nerdy role-playing game. He's like a [color=#3b78e2][i]total[/i][/color] stalker.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: What makes you think that?

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: He wants to be my Homecoming date. Like that's gonna happen. I've got a list of like ten other guys who I'd love to go with.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: A list?

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: Kind of like a pros and cons thing.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Tell me that isn't what it sounds like... Because it sounds like...
Before Emily can finish her sentence she sees the email attachment from Kimi.

nodes.speaker: Computer
nodes.text: Phil Ramirez. Pros: Hot! Plays guitar! Drives Mustang. Some DJ skills. Six-pack abs (did I mention 'hot'?). Senior = Prom potential.

nodes.speaker: Computer
nodes.text: Cons: Possible body spray user. 2.32 GPA. Crazy exes (at least three). Uses the term 'bro'. Senior = Gone next year.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: He... Sounds like a winner.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: Yeah... Except I heard a rumor he already started dating this older girl. And he's never said hi to me.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Maybe that means `you` have to say hi...
nodes.text_bbcode: Maybe that means [color=#3b78e2][i]you[/i][/color] have to say hi...

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: When? He's always surrounded in like a cone of dudes at school. I need to catch him at a party.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: Too bad we `never get invited.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Too bad we [color=#3b78e2][i]never get invited.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: But I'm pretty sure that doesn't really matter to you...
For one second, Emily imagines Ben at one of his parties, bored, looking for someone to talk to...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Actually I sort of wish we could go to a party too. Not that my dad would let me.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: For real?! There's hope for you yet! We are gonna make this `happen!`
nodes.text_bbcode: For real?! There's hope for you yet! We are gonna make this [color=#3b78e2][i]happen![/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: ...Somehow.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: Anyway, any adventures without me?
Emily thinks for a moment about her failure at swim practice... And about her encounter with Nick.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: Hello? Em, you there?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Sorry. Yeah. Nothing major.

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: All right, then. I'll see you tomorrow!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Good night.
Emily hangs up...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: What was I going to say...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: 'Hey, you know that guy who was driving the night Sara died? Well I bumped into him in the cafeteria!'
Emily gets into bed and tries to think about good things...
About swimming trophies... And that feel of the water when her body first knifes through it...
But mostly, she thinks of Ben.
Hey SHS Fans! This week's episode celebrates something special and dear to us...
We've been working for a long time on a Surviving High School `novel,` and it's finally releasing!
nodes.text_bbcode: We've been working for a long time on a Surviving High School [b]novel,[/b] and it's finally releasing!

nodes.text: Coming soon, `Surviving High School,` published by Poppy, will be available for purchase!
nodes.text_bbcode: Coming soon, [b]Surviving High School,[/b] published by Poppy, will be available for purchase!

nodes.text: You can even pre-order a copy of the book at the end of this episode!
So, without further ado, we present a treat... The first four chapters of the Surviving High School novel, adapted into SHS episode format!
In the photo room, Emily Kessler stands at the front of a long line for Student ID photos.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Okay, Emily. Remember to smile. Smile at all costs... You don't want to have an ugly student ID card like you did for `all` of middle school.
nodes.text_bbcode: Okay, Emily. Remember to smile. Smile at all costs... You don't want to have an ugly student ID card like you did for [color=#3b78e2][i]all[/i][/color] of middle school.

nodes.speaker: Photographer
nodes.text: All right, next.
Emily stands on a taped 'X' in front of the camera, trying to hold a smile.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Just smile...

nodes.speaker: Photographer
nodes.text: Uh, great. Hold it just like that.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Keep... Smiling!

nodes.speaker: Photographer
nodes.text: Oh... Wait, I'm pressing the wrong button.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Cheeks... Hurt!
`Click!`
nodes.text_bbcode: [b]Click![/b]

nodes.text: A few seconds later, the photographer hands Emily her new ID...

nodes.speaker: Photographer
nodes.text: Here you go...

nodes.text_bbcode: Two... This is [color=#3b78e2][i]your[/i][/color] homeroom... The place where you come to check-in, tell me how you're doing, and complain about your other classes.

nodes.speaker: Alicia
nodes.text: Juicy gossip on the rest of the faculty is appreciated and even welcomed. It's my first year here, so I'm going to need all the ammunition I can get.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Do you have a boyfriend?! Heh.

nodes.speaker: Alicia
nodes.text: Right. Number three... I may look like some starry-eyed innocent fresh out of grad school, but allow me to assure you that this kitty has fangs.

nodes.speaker: Alicia
nodes.text: Any more comments like that, and you may just find yourself transferred to homeroom with Mr. Upton...

nodes.speaker: Alicia
nodes.text: `His` first class of the year always starts with an informative `scared straight` talk with some very nice felons who I'm sure would `love` to meet you.
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#3b78e2][i]His[/i][/color] first class of the year always starts with an informative [color=#3b78e2][i]scared straight[/i][/color] talk with some very nice felons who I'm sure would [color=#3b78e2][i]love[/i][/color] to meet you.

nodes.text: The room is stone quiet.

nodes.speaker: Alicia
nodes.text: Excellent. I just know this is going to be an awesome year.
The girl next to Emily whispers... Almost to herself.

nodes.speaker: Jill
nodes.text: I `so` want to be her.
nodes.text_bbcode: I [color=#3b78e2][i]so[/i][/color] want to be her.

nodes.text: Emily nods.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Me too.
The rest of Emily's morning is a blur of classes... Uneventful with one exception...
In English class, a guy turns around, looks at her, and says...

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: You going to Ben Kale's place this Friday?
But then Emily realizes he's talking to the girls behind her.

nodes.speaker: Jenna
nodes.text: Ben Kale? I thought he got expelled or something.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: That was just some community service. He's back with a vengeance.

nodes.speaker: Hannah
nodes.text: You think you can get us into his party?

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Definitely. Hot girls are always welcome.
The girls giggle.

nodes.speaker: Jenna
nodes.text: We'll think about it.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: This must be what high school's like. I'll spend it worrying that everyone's judging me, when really it's the opposite. I'm invisible.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I guess I just... Don't exist...
